clearing_status.fact: The SEC formally extended compliance deadlines once (Release 34-102487, Feb 25 2025): cash to Dec 31 2026, repo to Jun 30 2027. As of the SEC Commissioner Uyeda August 2026 statement (sec.gov, Aug 7 2026), those remain the operative deadlines with no second extension, but SIFMA exemptive-relief requests (inter-affiliate and IIB extraterritorial) were published by the SEC on Apr 17 2026 with a May 29 2026 comment deadline, and remain pending.
clearing_status.rationale: One official one-year extension was granted (Feb 2025), satisfying rubric level 1's 'official extension granted' criterion; SIFMA and IIB exemptive-relief requests pending as of Apr-May 2026 further confirm level 1. No second formal deadline extension has been announced, so level 2 is not triggered.

plan_financing.fact: 10y JGB yield eased to 2.99% on Sept 18, 2026 (TradingEconomics), ~80-90bps above the ~2.1% level when Takaichi took office in Feb 2026, driven by fiscal stimulus and BOJ tightening concerns. The Sept 3 30-year auction cleared with BTC 3.79 vs. 12-month avg 3.52 (Bloomberg, Sept 3 2026); the Sept 1 10-year auction landed with 'average bid-to-cover and tail' (note.com). No failed auction or emergency BOJ operation observed. Takaichi's FY27 budgeting framework remains unspecified (MUFG Research, Jan 2026).
plan_financing.rationale: The yield rise far exceeds the 25bps threshold and the fiscal funding path for FY27 is unspecified, satisfying the UNCLEAR (1) criteria; however, all recent auctions cleared with BTC well above 2 and no emergency BOJ operation was triggered, precluding a DISORDERLY (2) rating.

dissent.view: Lazard (mid-year 2026) notes Takaichi 'tempered expectations for sizable fiscal stimulus' to reassure bond markets, implying partial stabilisation of fiscal concerns

Oxford Economics raised end-2026 10y JGB yield forecast to 2.8%, suggesting yield rise is partly BOJ-driven rather than purely fiscal-concern-driven, which could argue the fiscal-specific signal is weaker than the headline move implies

direct_lending_default.fact: Fitch Ratings reported the trailing 12-month US private credit default rate (inclusive of distressed exchanges and liability-management exercises, across ~1,300-1,500 borrowers) rose to 6.3% at end-August 2026, up from 6.1% in July and a prior record of 6.0% in April-May 2026. Source: Bloomberg, 14 Sep 2026 (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-14/us-private-credit-default-rate-hits-a-record-of-6-3-fitch-says); corroborated by Newsbreak/Benzinga and Epoch Times citing the same Fitch release.
direct_lending_default.rationale: Fitch's broad-definition PCDR (inclusive measure counting distressed exchanges and maturity extensions) printed 6.3% TTM through August 2026, a new record high surpassing the prior 6.1% in July; this is the controlling Fitch reading per the rubric and displaces the April 6.0% anchor. The rate has been above 6% continuously since April 2026 with August producing 14 default events—the highest monthly count in the trailing-year window—corroborating persistent middle-market credit stress.

dissent.view: Proskauer Private Credit Default Index: 2.51% in Q2 2026 (count-based, senior secured/unitranche, 716 loans, $195.6B). Materially lower due to narrower coverage and exclusion of many distressed-exchange events.
Moody's: 2025 private credit headline default rate 1.6%-4.7% excluding distressed restructurings; estimated ~65% of 2025 defaults were distressed exchanges/maturity extensions.

redemption_gates.fact: Fitch Ratings data (reported August 2026) shows 10 of 16 tracked non-traded BDCs breached their quarterly 5% repurchase caps in Q2 2026, with total redemption requests of $15.6 billion unfulfilled. Named funds enforcing gates include: Blackstone Private Credit Fund (BCRED, ~$79bn AUM, ~10% Q2 requests vs 5% cap), Ares Strategic Income Fund (14.4% Q2 requests, capped at 5%), Apollo Debt Solutions BDC (17% Q2 requests, capped at 5%), Blue Owl OBDC II ($1.6bn, repurchase program fully suspended in Feb 2026), Morgan Stanley North Haven Private Income Fund (11.6% Q2 requests), and Oaktree Strategic Credit Fund (6.8% Q1 requests, cap expanded). Sources: Fitch Ratings via angelinvestorsnetwork.com (Aug 20 2026); alternativecreditinvestor.com (Jun 27 2026); abfjournal.com (May 28 2026); altswire.com (May 17 2026).
redemption_gates.rationale: The rubric's level-2 threshold (>=3 of the largest funds gating, or combined AUM >$100bn) is far exceeded: 10 of 16 tracked BDCs hit their caps in the same quarter (Q2 2026), with BCRED alone at ~$79bn AUM and multiple other multi-billion-dollar funds (Ares, Apollo, Blue Owl, Morgan Stanley, Oaktree) simultaneously gating. No corroborating funding-market signal is required to override — the breadth (majority of Fitch's sample) and named-fund AUM aggregation well above $100bn makes this unambiguously WIDESPREAD.

dissent.view: Some analysts (CAIA, iCapital, CLA) characterise gate activation as 'funds operating as designed' rather than a stress event, noting gates are contractual features not credit deterioration signals, and that early Q3 2026 data (e.g. Golub GCRED cleared July tender in full at 4.8%) suggests possible peak.

new_imf_programs.fact: IMF Executive Board approved a new US$8.1 billion 48-month EFF for Ukraine on Feb 26 2026 (source: imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/02/26/pr-26066-ukraine); Argentina operates under a US$20-21bn EFF agreed in 2025 with a review cleared May 2026 (source: batimes.com.ar, May 22 2026); no confirmed new sovereign missed coupons or fresh defaults found in the Mar-Sep 2026 window.
new_imf_programs.rationale: Ukraine's new EFF (approved Feb 26 2026, active throughout the window) plus Argentina's ongoing EFF (review milestone May 2026) constitute 1-2 newly active IMF arrangements with no confirmed missed coupons, mapping to RISING (band 1); no evidence of >=3 sovereigns in new programs or default supports ruling out CLUSTER (band 2).

dissent.view: Ukraine EFF approval date (Feb 26 2026) falls just outside the strict trailing-6-month window (Mar 21 - Sep 21 2026), which could reduce the count to ~1 (Argentina continuation only) and support CALM (0)

china_ppi.fact: China PPI for industrial products increased 3.8% year-on-year in August 2026, per NBS data released 9 September 2026 (corroborated by People's Daily en.people.cn/n3/2026/0909/c90000-20497638.html and Vantage Markets vantagemarkets.com/market-news/china-cpi-ppi-august-energy-prices-september-9-2026/; prior month July was +3.5% per NBS official release stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202608/t20260810_1965017.html).
china_ppi.rationale: The rubric scores on the SIZE of the move regardless of sign; at +3.8% YoY China PPI is a notably positive print representing a sharp cost-push inflation signal that exports input-cost pressure globally, well above the near-zero baseline of early 2026. This is a material positive-side price-spillover reading.

trade_actions.fact: In the trailing 3 months: (1) USTR imposed a new 12.5% Section 301 forced-labor tariff on Chinese goods effective 24 July 2026 (China Briefing, 23 Jul 2026); (2) EU imposed definitive AD duties of 4.3%-45.3% on Chinese car/lorry tyres, 7 Jul 2026 (EC trade policy page); (3) EU raised ceramic tableware AD duties on China to 79% (amfori.org); (4) China expanded rare earth export controls to 10 US firms 22 Jun 2026 and 14 EU firms 24 Jul 2026 (tech-insider.org/MOFCOM); (5) China introduced drone export controls and entity sanctions 5 Aug 2026 (usahousinginformation.com). Total: >=5 new distinct measures across multiple major economies.
trade_actions.rationale: The rubric scores ESCALATING (2) at >=4 new measures OR a broad tariff round >=10% across a sector; the trailing 3 months produced at least 5 discrete measures including the 12.5% US Section 301 forced-labor tariff (a broad cross-sector round), EU sector-specific AD duties, and Chinese retaliatory export controls, clearly clearing both thresholds.

dissent.view: CRS (Aug 18 2026) frames the US-China relationship as still inside a managed negotiating track with trade/investment boards created in May 2026, suggesting escalation is bounded rather than open-ended.

license_flow.fact: As of mid-2026, China's MOFCOM operates a mandatory case-by-case export licensing regime for heavy-REE magnets (NdFeB with Dy/Tb, SmCo) imposed in April 2025. General licences exist but are limited to a small cohort of pre-cleared major exporters (JL MAG, San Huan, Yunsheng, first issued December 2025); they are 'not broadly available.' Processing times officially target 45 working days (~9 weeks) but in practice run 60-120 days for heavy-REE materials. The January 2026 licensing catalogue added new controls on samarium, gadolinium, and lutetium compounds. MOFCOM explicitly will not approve licences for military end-users. Trump threats of 200% tariffs in August 2026 over insufficient magnet supply confirm the slow-approval signal is market-corroborated. Sources: rare-earth-mining.com (Apr 2026), blog.gettransport.com (Jul 2026), china-briefing.com (Nov 2025 updated), certivo.com (Mar 2026), techtimes.com (May 2026), energy-solutions.co (verified 2026-08-27).
license_flow.rationale: The regime is unambiguously case-by-case (per-shipment licences required for controlled categories; general licences confined to named producers only), new categories were added to the control list within the trailing 3 months (Jan 2026 catalogue additions remain in effect), and processing times routinely exceed 30 days (60-120 days observed for heavy-REE). All three SLOWING triggers under rubric level 1 are met; no categorical denial to an entire country or sector-wide suspension of licensing issuance meets the FROZEN threshold.

dissent.view: One supplier case study (Mainrich) cites a 23-day approval for a straightforward EV-motor civilian order, implying some commercial shipments clear faster than the 60-120 day median reported elsewhere.

Rare Earth Exchanges cites licensing approval rates below 25% for European firms (Apr 2026), which could argue for a FROZEN reading for that bilateral segment, though no formal categorical denial order has been published.

truce_status.fact: China's one-year suspension of Oct-9-2025 rare-earth export controls remains nominally in force but expires November 10, 2026 — under 51 days away with no renewal announced. China added 10 US firms (incl. MP Materials, USA Rare Earth) to restrictions in June 2026 (Reuters) and maintains a rare-earth export ban on Japan which the US formally contests as a truce breach (NPR, 2026-09-17). Trump-Xi Washington summit to discuss renewal is scheduled for Sept 24. Source: The National News, 2026-09-21; NPR, 2026-09-17; Modern Diplomacy, 2026-08-21.
truce_status.rationale: The truce is <90 days from expiry with no confirmed renewal, and partial breaches (new entity-list additions to MP Materials/USA Rare Earth, Japan rare-earth ban) have been formally flagged by the US — squarely meeting the rubric's '1 = EXPIRING/fraying' threshold. Score 2 is not warranted because the suspension itself has not formally lapsed and controls have not been reimposed on US-bound shipments.

dissent.view: Truce still broadly holding: a senior US official (Feb 2026) confirmed it 'is still in effect'; ITIC (Sep 2026) notes China 'appears to be upholding its commitments' on general licenses even as license delays/denials persist at the company level.
Alperovitch/Silverado (Sep 21 2026) assess the 'uneasy truce is likely to continue' past the summit, implying extension expected — which would push score back toward 0.

re_blacklist.fact: On 22 June 2026, China MOFCOM issued Announcement No. 23 of 2026 adding 10 named US entities to its export-control list, explicitly including MP Materials Corp. and USA Rare Earth, Inc., alongside eight defence/aerospace firms (Red Cat Holdings, Teal Drones, Aveox, Oshkosh Defense, L3Harris Maritime Services, and others). The ban prohibits Chinese exporters from shipping dual-use items to the named entities and bars any third-country transfer of Chinese-origin dual-use items to them, effective immediately. Source: MOFCOM Announcement No. 23 of 2026, corroborated by Benchmark Mineral Intelligence (25 Jun 2026), Bloomberg (22 Jun 2026), Arnold & Porter advisory (2 Jul 2026), and SMM/metal.com (22 Jun 2026). Benchmark explicitly characterises the measure as 'entity-specific rather than a blanket restriction on rare earth exports to the US.'
re_blacklist.rationale: Two named US rare-earth producers (MP Materials and USA Rare Earth) are explicitly listed in a firm-specific MOFCOM announcement; the restriction targets 10 individually named companies, not a categorical class of US rare-earth producers or all US dual-use recipients, mapping squarely to rubric score 1. No evidence of a sector-wide or categorical ban (score 2) exists.

hree_premium.fact: China domestic dysprosium oxide ~$212-218/kg (CREIA index 262.0, Sept 17 2026); ex-China (USA Rare Earth indicative) ~$1,100/kg; Rare Earth Exchanges (Sept 17 2026) headline: 'dysprosium and terbium prices outside China can run 4-5x higher.' Argus data cited by Reuters (June 2026) also reports Dy/Tb ex-China at x4-x5. Benchmark Minerals (March 24 2026) pegged 2025 avg at 4.4x CIF N. America, trending higher through 2026.
hree_premium.rationale: Dividing the mid-point ex-China dysprosium price (~$1,100/kg) by the China domestic reference (~$215/kg) yields ~5.1x, consistent with the 4-5x range reported by multiple sources as of mid-to-late September 2026; the rubric asks for the approximate multiple, so 5.0 is the best single reading.

dissent.view: Metal.com/SMM H1 2026 review characterises heavy REE ex-China premium as only '30-40% over domestic Chinese levels' — far below all other sources and likely reflects FOB vs domestic spread rather than true CIF ex-China Western-buyer premium
Benchmark Minerals forecasts the multiple rising to 8.3x by 2027, implying the current 2026 reading is still in transition above the 4.4x 2025 baseline but not yet at the forecast peak

genius_impl.fact: The statutory July 18, 2026 deadline for GENIUS Act implementing final rules was missed by all seven required agencies (OCC, FDIC, Federal Reserve, NCUA, Treasury, FinCEN, OFAC). As of early September 2026, 'not a single final rule' has been issued across any of the 10 NPRMs filed, per the Chapman & Cutler rulemaking tracker and confirmed by Yahoo Finance/ABA Banking Journal (Sept 2026). The OCC Comptroller publicly committed to a final rule 'by November' at the Wyoming Blockchain Symposium on Aug 19, 2026. Treasury's NPRM on issuance/offer/sale was published Aug 18, 2026, with comments due Oct 19, 2026 — structurally precluding finalization before that date. Source: fdic.gov (Apr 7 2026 NPRM); federalregister.gov (Aug 18 2026 Treasury NPRM); yahoo.com/finance 'GENIUS Act Compliance Cliff' (early Sept 2026); chapman.com tracker (as of Jul 16 2026); occ.gov Bulletin 2026-3.
genius_impl.rationale: The rubric's Level 2 condition is 'deadline missed without final rules': the July 18, 2026 statutory deadline has passed with zero final rules promulgated across all seven required agencies, confirmed by multiple authoritative trackers as of September 2026. No court stay is needed to score 2 — the plain missed-deadline-without-final-rules criterion is fully satisfied.

dissent.view: Some sources (Chapman & Cutler tracker, Paradigm tracker) note agencies frequently miss statutory deadlines with limited practical consequences and that the Jan 18, 2027 effective date backstop remains operative, implying the overall framework is not in crisis — suggesting a softer read closer to '1' (gaps) rather than hard failure.

tech-insider.org characterises the situation as 'every major package still stuck at the proposal stage' but frames it as an administrative sequencing issue rather than a systemic breakdown, which could support a '1' (gaps) classification.

ai_revenue_gap.fact: Q2 2026 earnings (Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft): Google Cloud grew +82% YoY to $24.8B (accelerating from +63% in Q1); AWS grew +37% YoY to $42.2B (accelerating from +28% in Q1); Azure grew +43% YoY (accelerating from ~+40% in Q1). Meanwhile aggregate 2026 capex guidance was simultaneously raised: Amazon to ~$220B, Alphabet to $195-205B, Meta to $130-145B — combined ~$740-760B, up ~77% from ~$410B in 2025. Sources: fourweekmba.com citing Amazon/Alphabet/Microsoft Q2 2026 earnings releases; uncoveralpha.com citing Q2 2026 earnings; kucoin.com citing Alphabet Q2 2026 earnings (July 31 2026).
ai_revenue_gap.rationale: Capex growth (~77% YoY aggregate) materially exceeds cloud/AI-revenue growth (37-82% YoY by segment, but starting from a far smaller base — AI run rates still lag full capex by a wide margin per io-fund.com). However, all three major cloud units accelerated QoQ (Google Cloud: 63%->82%; AWS: 28%->37%; Azure: ~40%->43%), ruling out the QoQ deceleration or guidance-cut trigger required for a score of 2; the gap is wide but not widening on the revenue-momentum dimension, placing this squarely at rubric level 1.

dissent.view: io-fund.com (Aug 2026) notes that AI revenue run rates still lag capex 'by a wide degree' and Meta total revenue decelerated QoQ (33%->28% with Q3 guide implying ~22%), suggesting one hyperscaler (Meta) may be closer to a score-2 dynamic on its standalone AI-revenue trajectory versus capex.

bingx.com (Jul 31 2026) reports Amazon trailing-twelve-month FCF turned negative (-$7.6B) and Meta FCF fell 91%, framing the capex-versus-cash-conversion gap as a near-term financing risk rather than a pure revenue-momentum story.

gpu_refi_stress.fact: CoreWeave (CRWV) CDS spread hit ~855bps on July 29, 2026 implying a 50% five-year default probability on its GPU-backed debt, while JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, and SMBC were actively seeking to offload AI/data-center construction loans — some reportedly at a discount — due to concentration limits; CoreWeave carried a documented $4.2B 2026 refinancing wall on GPU-collateralized debt with depreciating collateral, though it subsequently closed an $8.5B DDTL (Q1), a $2B oversubscribed bond (May), a $1.5B bond (June), and a $2.6B DDTL 5.5 (Aug 10, 2026 SEC filing) without a confirmed default. Sources: TechTimes Jul 30 2026 (CDS); Tech Newsday/ResultSense May 6 2026 (bank offloading); eMarketer May 5 2026 (discount); Dave Friedman Substack Apr 19 2026 ($4.2B wall); SEC EDGAR Aug 10 2026 CRWV 8-K (DDTL 5.5 close).
gpu_refi_stress.rationale: Named borrower (CoreWeave) faces a documented refinancing wall on GPU-backed debt with CDS spreads at deeply distressed levels (~855bps/50% 5yr PD) and major banks are actively offloading AI data-center debt, some at a discount — all hallmarks of rubric level 1 SIGNS. No confirmed default, distressed exchange, or failed refinancing has occurred as of the research date, so level 2 ACUTE is not warranted.

cmbs_office_delinq.fact: Trepp CMBS office delinquency rate hit a new all-time high of 11.76% in October 2025, per CommercialSearch/Trepp monthly report (commercialsearch.com, last updated July 31, 2026 with 2025 data). The overall Trepp CMBS DQ rate was 7.85% in August 2026 with office continuing to post increases (Multifamily Dive, Sept. 16, 2026), but no explicit Trepp office-only percentage for 2026 months was surfaced.
cmbs_office_delinq.rationale: The last hard Trepp office delinquency print is 11.76% (Oct 2025 ATH); KBRA's competing universe showed 13.9% in Jan 2026 and 12.8% in Feb 2026, suggesting the Trepp office rate likely migrated higher into 2026. Confidence is medium because the office-specific Trepp figure for 2026 months was not directly published in accessible sources, requiring reliance on the Oct 2025 ATH as the anchor. [vintage guard: new read is 2025-10 data but the prior applied value was 2026-03 data; kept the newer vintage]

dissent.view: KBRA-rated CMBS office delinquency rate hit 13.9% in January 2026 (driven by One New York Plaza $835M transfer to special servicer) then fell to 12.8% in February 2026 after modification/extension
S&P Global Ratings noted the CMBS office delinquency rate surpassed 10.5% in January 2026

regional_bank_stress.fact: Five US banks failed in 2026 YTD per FDIC (fdic.gov/resources/resolutions/bank-failures/in-brief/2026): Metropolitan Capital Bank & Trust (Jan 30, $261M assets, CRE/real-estate loan exposure documented by FDIC OIG review dated May 29 2026 and Bisnow reporting); Community Bank and Trust-West Georgia (May 1, $288M assets, preceded by FDIC enforcement action April 2026); Kentland FSL (July, tiny); Small Business Bank Lenexa KS (July, ~$73M); Tioga-Franklin Savings Bank (Aug 21, $68M). In the trailing 6 months (Mar 21-Sep 21 2026), 4 failures occurred. Of these, 1-2 have CRE/real-estate exposure explicitly cited as a contributing factor; the remainder are attributed to general capital erosion and operating deficiencies. No failure exceeded $10B in assets and no coordinated interagency CRE-specific supervisory action was identified.
regional_bank_stress.rationale: With 1-2 failures in the trailing 6-month window where FDIC/credible sources explicitly cite CRE/real-estate exposure as a contributing factor (Metropolitan Capital via FDIC OIG May 2026, Community Bank & Trust-West Georgia via FDIC enforcement action), and all failures well below $10B with no interagency CRE emergency action, the rubric maps to ISOLATED (score=1). The broader 4-failure count in the window does not clear the CLUSTER bar because CRE is only explicitly attributed to 1-2 of them, with reporting characterizing the pattern as idiosyncratic community bank operating failures rather than a CRE-driven systemic event.

govt_stability.fact: The Second Lecornu minority government (formed 10 Oct 2025) is the incumbent government of France as of 17 Sep 2026. It survived multiple no-confidence votes in Jan-Feb 2026 (LFI motion on 23 Jan received 269 votes vs 288 needed; RN motion received fewer) after invoking Article 49.3 to pass the 2026 budget revenue section. Bloomberg, 17 Sep 2026, reports Lecornu is now preparing a 2027 budget bill that 'risks toppling the government just ahead of presidential elections,' confirming the government is still in office but acutely fragile. Sources: Reuters/Al Jazeera 14 Jan 2026; Euronews/Al Jazeera 23 Jan - 2 Feb 2026; Wikipedia 'Lecornu governments'; Bloomberg 17 Sep 2026.
govt_stability.rationale: Lecornu's government is a minority coalition in a hung parliament (no working majority) that has relied on Article 49.3 and survived multiple no-confidence votes to govern — a textbook rubric-1 scenario. No dissolution or PM resignation has occurred, ruling out rubric 2; the absence of a working majority rules out rubric 0.

rating_action.fact: Fitch cut France AA- → A+ (stable outlook) on ~12 Sept 2025 (Euronews/Bloomberg); S&P cut France AA- → A+ (stable outlook) on ~17 Oct 2025 (Euronews); Moody's kept Aa3 but moved outlook to Negative on 25 Oct 2025 (France24). Fitch affirmed A+/Stable 28 Aug 2026; S&P affirmed A+ May 2026. All three cuts/outlook changes fall within trailing 12 months of 2026-09-21.
rating_action.rationale: Two of the three major agencies (Fitch and S&P) executed outright one-notch rating cuts within the trailing 12-month window (Sept–Oct 2025), satisfying rubric band 2 (actual rating cut). Moody's additionally shifted to Negative outlook in the same window, reinforcing the most severe band.

subprime_auto_dpd.fact: Fitch Ratings subprime auto ABS 60+ day delinquency rate was 5.67% in June 2026, down 64 basis points year over year, per Kaplan Collection Agency citing Fitch (published ~Sept 2026). Peak was 6.90% in January 2026 (32-year record). Competing source (ankso.blog, updated Aug 31 2026) cites 5.49% as of May 2026.
subprime_auto_dpd.rationale: The Fitch ABS index is the canonical primary source for subprime auto 60+ DPD; the June 2026 reading of 5.67% is the latest monthly figure available and maps directly to the rubric's requested metric. The seasonal post-tax-refund decline from the January record high is typical and does not change the structurally elevated character of the rate.

dissent.view: 5.49% as of May 2026 (lowest since May 2024) per Fitch data cited by ankso.blog (updated Aug 31, 2026) — one month earlier than the Kaplan June figure

bnpl_delinq.fact: Affirm Q4 FY2026 (three months ended June 30, 2026) 30+ DPD on monthly installment loans (ex-Peloton, ex-Pay in X) was 2.5%, down from 2.7-2.8% in the prior three quarters but up modestly YoY vs ~2.4% at FY2024 year-end; the full FY2026 delinquency curve 'tracked slightly above FY2025.' Sector BNPL charge-offs remain ~1.8-2% per chargeflow/CFPB. Sources: Affirm FQ4 FY2026 IR release (Aug 27 2026) via Yahoo Finance; Affirm FQ2'26 Shareholder Letter (Feb 2026) noting +18 bps YoY to 2.7%; Richmond Fed EB-26-05 (Mar 2026).
bnpl_delinq.rationale: Affirm 30+ DPD rose ~10-18 bps YoY across FY2026 quarters — clearly up YoY but far below the 100-bps threshold for level 2; sector charge-offs at ~1.8-2% are well under the 3% cap, placing the indicator squarely in rubric band 1 (RISING, charge-offs contained).

dissent.view: Richmond Fed (Mar 2026) cites only 'indicative evidence' of rising late payments from surveys, stopping short of confirming hard delinquency deterioration; some analysts note FQ4 improvement to 2.5% could signal stabilisation.

dollar_reserve_share.fact: IMF COFER Data Brief (data.imf.org, published 2026-06-30): 'The share of US dollar holdings in foreign exchange reserves increased to 57.13 percent in 2026Q1, from 56.42 percent in 2025Q4.'
dollar_reserve_share.rationale: The rubric calls for the latest USD share of allocated global FX reserves as a percent; the IMF COFER 2026Q1 release is the most recent official quarterly publication, reporting exactly 57.13%. This maps directly and mechanically to the indicator with no ambiguity.

dissent.view: coferdata.com tracker displays USD share at 56.77%, consistent with the prior 2025Q4 IMF release (Mar 27 2026 brief), not the latest 2026Q1 figure

weaponization_event.fact: At the 18th BRICS Summit (New Delhi, 12-13 Sep 2026), leaders adopted the New Delhi Declaration formally endorsing BRICS Pay - 'a decentralized payment messaging ecosystem designed to route cross-border transactions through national systems rather than the dollar-denominated SWIFT network' - and addressed the gold-backed BRICS Unit token pilot; crucially, 'BRICS Pay is not a currency and does not replace the dollar as a reserve asset' (Eastern Herald, 12 Sep 2026). No new sovereign reserve seizure occurred: Russian assets remain frozen under the pre-existing 2022 G7/EU freeze, with EU permanent-seizure proposals still debated but not enacted as of Sep 2026 (Brookings, Jun 2025; CFR, Nov 2025).
weaponization_event.rationale: The formal adoption of BRICS Pay at the New Delhi Declaration (Sep 12, 2026) and the BRICS Unit pilot constitute new non-dollar settlement agreements and launches, squarely mapping to rubric level 1 (TALK/agreements). No new sovereign reserve freeze or operationally transformative reserve settlement shift by a major economy has been confirmed, so the evidence does not reach level 2.

dissent.view: Some sources (informedclearly.com, watcher.guru) characterise BRICS Pay as already 'operational' and claim intra-bloc local-currency trade has surpassed 67%, suggesting a more advanced de-dollarisation that could edge toward ACTION; however these are non-primary, speculative outlets and the New Delhi Declaration language and RBI/EBC reporting confirm BRICS Pay remains a payment messaging layer, not a reserve settlement system replacement.

insurer_exits.fact: NAIC's August 5, 2026 first-of-its-kind MCAS report ('Examining Homeowner Property Insurance Market Dynamics: An Assessment of Countrywide State-Level Data From 2018 to 2024') found company-initiated non-renewal rates rose 96%-216% across ALL FOUR U.S. geographic regions (Northeast, Southeast, Midwest, West) from 2018-2024, with the steepest increases in the West (>3x). The Southeast region showed a continuous net decline in carrier count across the full 7-year period (-4%). Florida non-renewed 3.35% of policies in 2024 (highest nationally, 1.7x 2018 rate); California non-renewed 3.18% (3.9x its 2018 rate). Named states with active non-renewal/exit stress include CA, FL, LA, TX, CO, GA, OK - at minimum 7 states per contemporaneous reporting (Insurance Journal, rollingout.com, climatecosmos.com). The market is described as 'overall operationally robust but nonetheless under pressure and exhibiting signs of stress.' No confirmed full exit of a top-10 insurer from an entire major state in 2026; Citizens FL policy count fell from 1.42M (Oct 2023) to ~385K-395K (Jan 2026) showing private-market re-entry in FL. (Primary source: NAIC MCAS report, naic.org, Aug 5 2026; supporting: CNBC Aug 6 2026, beinsure.com Aug 12 2026)
insurer_exits.rationale: Non-renewal waves are documented across all four NAIC regions with at least 7 named states experiencing elevated non-renewals/partial exits - firmly in the 5-15 state RISING band - but the NAIC characterizes the national market as 'operationally strong overall' with improved 2024 underwriting results and no confirmed top-10 insurer full-state exit in 2026, precluding the ACCELERATING threshold of >15 states or a full top-10 exit.

dissent.view: S&P Global Market Intelligence shows U.S. effective approved homeowners rate change collapsed to just 1.8% through July 2026 (from 13.6% in 2024), suggesting material market stabilization that could argue toward STABLE in some geographies
Climate Cosmos (June 2026) lists 13 named states with active non-renewal drops, which if treated as a discrete state count would approach or exceed the ACCELERATING rubric threshold of >15

ss_reform_news.fact: The 2026 Social Security Trustees Report (released June 9, 2026; primary source: ssa.gov/oact/trsum/) projects OASI trust fund depletion in Q4 2032 -- one quarter earlier than the prior report -- with only 78% of scheduled benefits payable thereafter. No legislation enacting benefit cuts or restoring solvency has been enacted; multiple bills (Bipartisan Social Security Commission Act H.R. 9187, PROMISE Act introduced July 14, 2026) are proposed but none passed.
ss_reform_news.rationale: The trustees report worsened the depletion date (2033 -> 2032) and the 75-year actuarial deficit widened to 4.42% of taxable payroll, squarely satisfying rubric band 1 (depletion date worsened, reform actively debated). No automatic cut has been triggered and no legislation enacting cuts has been signed, so band 2 is not met.

dissent.view: AARP/CRS report combined OASDI depletion unchanged at 2034 (Q3 2034), framing the headline as 'no change' vs. the OASI-only 2032 worsening; the distinction is real but both readings confirm no enacted cuts.

pension_leverage_event.fact: ESMA's June 2026 TRV article on LDI funds (ESMA50-1949966494-4208, published 23 June 2026) finds that 'the ability of funds to meet liquidity demands has improved compared to September 2022' and that the liquidity shortfall under stress declined from €9bn to €3bn (end-2024 data), driven by lower leveraged exposures and a smaller segment NAV (€113bn vs €130bn at the 2022 crisis). Concurrently, TPR's Market Oversight report confirms LDI managers have raised rate buffers to ~300 bps (vs ~150 bps pre-2022) and that daily volatility in leveraged LDI assets is now more than 50% lower than end-2021, with no margin-call episode or forced gilt selling reported in 2025-2026. Source: ESMA (https://www.esma.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2026-06/ESMA50-1949966494-4208_LDI_funds_-_recent_developments_and_methods_for_liquidity_stress_testing_0.pdf) and TPR (https://www.thepensionsregulator.gov.uk/en/document-library/research-and-analysis/market-oversight-how-well-pension-schemes-are-prepared-for-ldi-risk).
pension_leverage_event.rationale: Both ESMA (June 2026) and TPR confirm LDI buffers are materially stronger (~300 bps headroom) and no margin-call episode or forced gilt selling has occurred; this maps cleanly to Rubric 0 (NONE: LDI buffers adequate, no margin stress). No regulator has flagged active liquidity stress in 2025-2026, and there is no evidence of a blowup episode.

funded_ratio.fact: Milliman 100 Public Pension Funding Index (PPFI): funded ratio of 88.2% as of July 31, 2026, covering the 100 largest U.S. public defined benefit plans; assets $6.095T vs. TPL $6.911T. Source: Milliman PPFI August 2026 release (businesswire.com/news/home/20260827829119).
funded_ratio.rationale: The Milliman PPFI is the canonical monthly mark-to-market index for the 100 largest U.S. public pensions, directly satisfying the rubric; 88.2 is the most recently published figure as of the research date. Equable Institute's broader FY2026 projection of 85.0% covers 253 systems including smaller, weaker plans, explaining the ~3pp gap.

dissent.view: Equable Institute 'State of Pensions 2026' (July 23, 2026) projects a national average funded ratio of 85.0% for FY2026 across 253 statewide and municipal systems — a broader and slightly lower-quality universe than Milliman's top-100 sample.
